# 2. Identity is generated by the domain

## Context

Two ways to give a new aggregate its id: ask the persistence layer (auto-increment, a `nextIdentity()` round trip to the repository) or let the domain pick one. The first ties the creation of an aggregate to an infrastructure call, means an aggregate cannot exist before it is stored, and puts an `async` in the middle of what is otherwise pure business logic.

## Decision

An aggregate picks its own identity when it is created: `Id.generate()` ([`Id.ts`](../../src/Contexts/@SharedKernel/Domain/Utils/Id.ts)), a UUID v4, inside `Note.create()` / `Account.register()`. Repositories only `findById` and `save`; there is no `nextIdentity()` on any port.

## Consequences

- `Note.create()` is synchronous and testable without a repository.
- The id is known before the first write, so the domain event recorded at creation carries it, and a command can answer with it immediately.
- Ids are opaque strings; nothing in the domain depends on them being sortable or sequential.
- Domain tests cannot assert a fixed id; they read it from the created aggregate (`note._id.value`).

## When to revisit

If a store required its own key format (a sequence, a composite key), the port would grow a `nextIdentity()` again and `create()` would take the id as a parameter — the shape Notes had before this decision, kept in the history.
